title: Hyperparameter Optimization via Budget Allocation in Lipschitz Spaces
abstract: arXiv:2510.10605v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Hyperparameter optimization and model selection often require allocating a limited evaluation budget across many candidate configurations, where performance improves with additional training or resources. We study this setting when each configuration has an unknown performance curve over budget. Similarity between configurations induces similarity between their curves, capturing geometric structure in the search space. We formalize the resulting decision problem as Unknown Value Probing and propose budget allocation strategies that combine principled exploration of the configuration space with value-informed concentration on regions supported by observed evidence. We prove worst-case approximation guarantees for our approach and show these guarantees are near-optimal by matching corresponding hardness barriers. Extensive experiments on large benchmark suites spanning more than 250 experimental settings demonstrate consistent gains ov

translated_title: 基于Lipschitz空间中预算分配的超参数优化
translated_abstract: 超参数优化和模型选择通常需要在多个候选配置之间分配有限的评估预算，其中性能会随着额外的训练或资源的增加而提升。我们研究每个配置在预算上具有未知性能曲线的场景。配置之间的相似性会导致其曲线之间的相似性，从而捕捉搜索空间中的几何结构。我们将由此产生的决策问题形式化为“未知值探测”，并提出了结合对配置空间进行原则性探索与基于观测证据的价值导向集中策略的预算分配方法。我们为该方法证明了最坏情况近似保证，并通过匹配相应的难度障碍证明这些保证接近最优。在涵盖250多个实验设置的大规模基准套件上的大量实验表明了一致的性能提升。
tldr: 该论文将超参数优化形式化为“未知值探测”决策问题，提出了在Lipschitz空间结构下结合探索与价值导向集中的预算分配策略，证明了接近最优的最坏情况近似保证，并在250多个实验设置中取得了一致的性能提升。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes hyperparameter optimization as an Unknown Value Probing problem and proposes budget allocation strategies with near-optimal worst-case approximation guarantees in Lipschitz spaces, demonstrating consistent gains across over 250 experimental settings.
